Validate a custom scanner against reviewed cases

Source: R/validate-scanner.R
validate_scanner.Rd

validate_scanner() runs a scanner() on the retained evidence of each reviewed case that targets it and compares the result with the adjudicated judgment. It reports development and test cases separately, and it keeps cases that cannot be scored out of every rate. It never calls a model and changes neither the saved findings nor the review decisions.

Usage

validate_scanner(scanner, examples, unit = "evidence")

Arguments

scanner

A scanner().

examples

A scanner example set from review_examples(). Cases that target another scanner are left out.

unit

"evidence" (the default) or "trajectory".

Value

A list with two tibbles.

summary has one row per split, always development then test: scan, scan_version, n_cases, scored, true_positive, false_positive, false_negative, true_negative, precision with precision_denominator (flagged scored cases), recall with recall_denominator (reviewed-positive scored cases), precision_note and recall_note, scanner_unassessed with its parts insufficient_evidence, not_applicable, and execution_failure, reviewer_uncertain, reviewer_insufficient_capture, not_adjudicated, and unreviewed_findings. A rate with a zero denominator is NA and its note says why.

cases has one row per case: case (its position in examples$cases), case_id, split, group, trajectory_id, judgment, reviewed ("positive", "negative", or NA), assessment and assessment_reason from the scanner, flagged, outcome, count of agreeing findings, the case's operator, target, and whether its predicate passed, scan_version and the reviewed_scan_version the reviewer saw, the review evidence (review_finding_id, review_event_ids, review_turn_ids, decision_ids, snapshot_id, revision_id), and what the scanner cited (finding_ids for the agreeing findings, other_finding_ids for its other findings in the trajectory, and scanner_event_ids for every event it cited there, and finding_keys and other_finding_keys, the revision-independent identities the summary counts by). A rerun finding that cites the same turn and events as a saved finding of the scan carries that saved identifier, the one review_finding_id uses; a finding the saved analysis does not hold, such as one a new version adds, keeps an identifier from the rerun that starts with "rerun/". outcome is true_positive, false_positive, false_negative, true_negative, or one of the unscored categories.

Details

A case is reviewed positive when its active decision is "confirmed" or "missed", and reviewed negative when it is "rejected". A case is scored only when it has one such decision and the scanner assessed the trajectory. The other cases are counted separately and are never treated as negatives:

  • scanner_unassessed: the scanner reported insufficient_evidence or not_applicable, or failed (execution_failure). Each has its own count. This category comes first, whatever the review says, so every scanner failure is counted.

  • reviewer_uncertain and reviewer_insufficient_capture: the reviewer could not judge the evidence.

  • not_adjudicated: the case is unreviewed, or has several active decisions that nobody has adjudicated.

Every case has exactly one outcome, so the scored and unscored counts add up to n_cases.

Unit of agreement

The unit is the reviewed case. With unit = "evidence" (the default) the scanner agrees with a case only through findings that cite the case's evidence: a finding counts when it shares an event with the case's event_ids and, when the case names turns, lies in one of its turn_ids. A case that cites no evidence is a whole-trajectory judgment, and any finding in the trajectory counts. Findings elsewhere in the trajectory are not scored for that case. unreviewed_findings counts the findings in the split's trajectories that agree with no scored case: no positive or negative judgment covers them, either because no case cites them or because the cases that do are uncertain, insufficient, unreviewed, or disputed. They are neither true nor false positives. With unit = "trajectory" any finding in the trajectory counts for every case, whatever evidence the case cites. Use it only when each trajectory has one case, since two cases on one trajectory would both be scored against the same flag.

Development and test cases

Development cases are for building the scanner: read its false positives and false negatives, change the function or its settings, and run again. Test cases are held out. Look at them once the scanner is settled, and do not change the scanner in response to them; a test result that has guided a change is a development result. The function reports both and tunes nothing. A rate measures agreement with these reviewed cases only. It is not an estimate for unreviewed traffic, and it says nothing about the quality of the application's answers.
